articles.title: Veja como comprar ingressos para a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027, no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: A Fifa divulgou nesta sexta-feira (13) que o preço inicial dos ingressos será de R$ 30, com direito a meia-entrada, seguindo a legislação brasileira.
articles.summary: A Fifa divulgou nesta sexta-feira (13) que o preço inicial dos ingressos será de R$ 30, com direito a meia-entrada, seguindo a legislação brasileira.
articles.body:
Sorteio dos grupos da Copa do Mundo feminina será dia 11 de dezembro, no Museu de Arte Moderna, no Rio — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A Fifa divulgou os detalhes da venda de ingressos para a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027.

O primeiro passo é abrir o computador, ir para a página e fazer o cadastro para comprar os ingressos. A Myriam, a Karla e o Liam, filho delas, já fizeram isso. A partir das 10h do dia 1º de dezembro começa a parte mais divertida: escolher os jogos e garantir os lugares.

É que o Liam nasceu no Brasil, a Karla também, mas a Myriam é francesa. A boa notícia para essa família é que vai dar para ver o Brasil, a França e muitas outras seleções nos 64 jogos da Copa. A Fifa divulgou nesta sexta-feira (13) que o preço inicial dos ingressos será de R$ 30, com direito a meia-entrada, seguindo a legislação brasileira.

A diretora executiva de futebol feminino da Fifa, Sarai Bareman, disse que para eles é importante que seja um evento no Brasil e para o Brasil; que todos tenham condições de pagar e fazer parte de uma celebração incrível do futebol no país.

Nessa primeira fase de vendas, também há três opções de pacotes de ingressos, que não incluem a final e a decisão de terceiro lugar:

o "Passaporte Flex" permite ao torcedor comprar um combo de três ingressos com direito a um jogo do Brasil na primeira fase ou uma semifinal;

já o "Passaporte Arena" dá direito a todas as partidas de um mesmo estádio até as quartas de final, com um desconto de 27%;

a terceira opção de pacote é para os jogos do Brasil na fase de grupos. O “Passaporte Seleção Brasileira” contempla a partida de abertura da Copa no Maracanã, no dia 24 de junho, a de Itaquera, em São Paulo, no dia 29, e a de Brasília, no Mané Garrincha, no dia 4 de julho. Vai dar para ver tudo isso nos estádios pagando R$ 205.

"É possível viver a emoção sem gastar tanto dinheiro, especialmente com criança”, diz Myriam.

articles.title: Asalto violento en casa de Matías Dituro mientras llegaba con sus hijos: "Fueron minutos de auténtico terror"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista llegó con familia cuando los ladrones habían accedido a su domicilio y una llamada de alerta de su mujer evitó que entraran en la vivienda
articles.summary: El futbolista llegó con familia cuando los ladrones habían accedido a su domicilio y una llamada de alerta de su mujer evitó que entraran en la vivienda
articles.body: Matías Dituro ha sido víctima de un robo en su domicilio particular. Una experiencia traumática que se tornó en auténtica pesadilla, como ha relatado el propio portero y capitán del Elche, a través de un comunicado en su cuenta de Instagram. Apenas cuatro minutos separaron a Matías Dituro y a sus hijos de cruzarse cara a cara con los ladrones que asaltaron su domicilio este jueves. El argentino llegaba a casa a las 20:49 horas junto a los pequeños, de seis y ocho años, cuando la llamada providencial de su mujer le alertó de que tres encapuchados acababan de irrumpir violentamente en el interior. Ante la tensión del momento, los niños rompieron a llorar y pidieron a su padre que no se bajara del coche y huyeran de allí. Quiero compartir con todos lo que vivimos anoche, no solo por desahogo, sino también para alertar a nuestros vecinos. Ayer, sobre las 20:45, tres personas encapuchadas y con herramientas irrumpieron de forma violenta en nuestra vivienda para robar, mientras una cuarta persona permanecía fuera vigilando y avisando si llegaba alguien. A las 20:49 llegué a casa con mis dos hijos, de 6 y 8 años, sin saber que los delincuentes seguían dentro. En ese preciso momento recibí la llamada de mi mujer avisándome de lo que estaba ocurriendo. Gracias a ese aviso y a la rápida actuación de un vecino, que escuchó los ruidos y comprobó en sus cámaras que estaban entrando en nuestra casa, no llegamos a entrar. Mis hijos rompieron a llorar, suplicándome que no me bajara del coche y que nos fuéramos de allí. Fueron unos minutos de auténtico terror que nunca olvidaremos. Los ladrones huyeron poco después, dejando nuestra casa completamente destrozada y llevándose parte de nuestras pertenencias. Lo material se puede recuperar; la tranquilidad y la sensación de seguridad en nuestro hogar no será tan fácil. Quiero agradecer de corazón a nuestro vecino por su rápida reacción y a todas las personas que nos están mostrando su apoyo. Gracias a esa llamada, hoy podemos decir que estamos todos bien. Confío en que las autoridades puedan identificar a los responsables y que respondan por el daño que han causado. Gracias a todos por su apoyo. Nuestra familia está bien, y eso es, sin duda, lo más importante.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino fought back tears, but doubts about his long-term USMNT commitment will linger
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino says he never planned to leave the USMNT so soon. But Manchester United came calling, leaving behind an improved American program and an...
articles.body:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — No matter how many times Mauricio Pochettino says he was in it for the long run, cynics will probably never accept his second term as U.S. coach was ever going to last through the 2030 World Cup.

Four years is an eternity in the life of a high-end boss accustomed to the 90-minute dopamine rush of the European club scene.

And on Friday, just 102 days after signing a four-year contract to continue the productive work he began in the fall of 2024 and carried through this summer's World Cup, Pochettino struggled to hold back tears at a news conference announcing he will depart next week to become Manchester United's head coach .

"I'm talking with my heart," he said while choking up.

His U.S. farewell will come after the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti on Saturday in Miami and Tuesday in Cincinnati. Then it's off to Old Trafford.

A suitor with less prestige might not have drawn him away from what he called "an amazing project" with the U.S.

But this wasn't just any suitor; it was Manchester bloody, freakin' United — a club that had spoken to Pochettino on three other occasions over the years and now is in desperate need of help amid its worst start in 40 years.

"I never said that I want to go back" to Europe, Pochettino said of suggestions he wasn't going to stay with the U.S. until 2030. "They know not too many opportunities can happen in your career like Manchester United. And of course, when that arrives, it's difficult to turn down that situation. But what I want to make clear, when we decide [to re-sign] together to extend our commitment," he was looking to 2030.

With a portfolio that includes a Champions League runner-up medal at Tottenham Hotspur, plus spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, Pochettino was commonly mentioned during his U.S. tenure as a possible replacement somewhere in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A or the other major European circuits.

Tottenham and AC Milan were reportedly pursuing him in his first 18 months on the job. And while he wouldn't have thumbed his nose at either club, the World Cup — his first World Cup as a coach — was on the horizon. He wasn't going to leave his U.S. bosses hanging.

Now it was different. Not only was United calling, but he had left the U.S. program in a good place and with the luxury of a long run-up to major competition and ultimately the next World Cup.

Pochettino said working for the U.S. was "a project and a program we were evolving together. That is why it makes it more difficult — a decision that, in some part, is a very sad decision, and in another part, we are professional and we need also to try to find the next step and try to make your dreams come true."

Pochettino aimed to make U.S. dreams come true this summer, though he fell short of getting beyond the World Cup's Round of 16 — the frustratingly typical American exit ramp.

He is, though, leaving the program in a much better place than it was when he arrived — with greater depth, a stronger culture, a pleasant playing style and heightened confidence and pride. Playing the World Cup on home soil, the U.S. performance (until the Belgium elimination match) captured hearts and elevated enthusiasm in not just the program but soccer at large.

"We have a team with great momentum. … Mauricio and his staff have raised the standard," chief executive J.T. Batson said. "The belief of what's possible for soccer in this country has never been higher."

There is, though, a lingering sense that Batson and his colleagues should have seen this coming, if not after 102 days but in the coming months. Pochettino is Argentine, but he's very much European, and he's very much a club coach at heart.

The USSF was smart enough to include a $10 million release clause in Pochettino's contract — a figure United must fork over to the USSF.

"Those funds are available for us to invest to make the biggest impact on our goals [and] making sure we have the resources to achieve our goals, including have a world-class coach," Batson said.

In other words, if another big pile of cash is needed to secure the next coach, the USSF will tap into it. Pochettino earned about $6 million, a USSF record. Getting him on board two years ago, though, was made possible by outside benefactors.

In the sign of the times in sports, Pochettino gave thanks to hedge-fund manager Scott Goodwin, who, along with billionaire Ken Griffin, helped buffer his salary. It's unclear whether the benefactors will ask the USSF for a return on their investment, so to speak, or continue bolstering the federation's efforts.

The coaching search, led by Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, will commence right away. Emma Hayes, the gold medal-winning women's coach, will assist. Steve Cherundolo — the under-23 coach prepping the 2028 Olympic team and a possible senior candidate — will handle a low-key camp without European players next month. The full squad won't regather until mid-March.

"Our ambition is high," Batson said, "and we believe this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world."

It's unclear if, by March, the new boss will be in place. But Pochettino could keep the momentum going by leading the U.S. to that Nations League's final four — a place it's been in each of the previous four editions of the regional tournament.

He might be a lame duck, but Pochettino insisted he won't let his mind wander to the massive challenge awaiting him in Manchester. On Friday, he repeatedly said he and the U.S. team's focus is on the Haiti matches.

"For sure, they are going to perform," he said. "We are very optimistic, and I think it's a very natural way to finish our partnership."

Given his abrupt departure, getting the most out of the team is the least he could do.

articles.title: Walsall: 'Some clubs in EFL beggar belief', says Saddlers' Pomlett
articles.summary: Walsall co-chairman Leigh Pomlett sends out a powerful response to the independent State of the Game report.
articles.body:
Walsall co-chairman Leigh Pomlett has given a powerful response to the independent State of the Game report by suggesting some clubs "beggar belief" in the way they operate.

The revelation of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) in its first report that 94% of clubs made losses in the 2025-26 season suggested the majority of clubs were living "on the edge of financial disaster".

Pomlett told BBC Radio WM at a Walsall fans' forum at Bescot Stadium just how serious football's financial problems are. And, although he stressed that the Saddlers are better run than most, the League Two promotion contenders will still have to make significant cuts in spending to qualify for an IFR operating licence in future.

"The State of the Game report came out a couple of weeks ago," he said. "A report that has come out from the independent regulator. It is a huge report and I have, for my sins, read all 260 pages of it.

"It goes into huge detail and, for the first time ever, is about the state of English football, right from the Premier League to the National League.

"Football is in a shocking state. Some clubs would still lose money even if they paid their players nothing. That is a fact. Some clubs will have to radically change what they do."

Majority of clubs on edge of 'financial disaster' - regulator

"Compared to some clubs, we at Walsall are in a very good state of health but it's still tough - just a lot less tough than it will be for some other clubs in the EFL who just beggar belief.

"We are at times accused of lack of ambition for not being able to buy this or that player, but the priority is still to make the club sustainable."

In a week when fellow Midlands-based League Two club Shrewsbury Town were taken over by new American owners , Pomlett warns that the scope for any club looking to speculate to accumulate will have to be drastically toned down if the regulator deduces they are spending money they have not got.

"The losses from the top to the bottom are massive," said Pomlett.

"Clubs who are losing an absolute fortune every week will not be allowed to continue like that.

"Thirty-three clubs do not have enough cash to survive a month. That's incredible.

"The losses being made in League One, League Two and the National League are enormous, but some of the Premier League and Championship losses are mind-boggling.

"The regulator is not going to let us carry on like that.

"We're on the brink of the biggest change in the football industry that we've seen since the Premier League was first formed."

After the BBC Radio WM Football Phone-In slot, a fuller recording of the Fans Forum will be posted on Sounds at 19:00 GMT.

articles.title: Afcon 2027 qualifying: Nigeria, Egypt and Morocco win but Tunisia fall to defeat
articles.summary: Nigeria beat Tanzania to boost their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Mohamed Salah scores twice as Egypt cruise to victory over Malawi.
articles.body:
Tolu Arokodare was the hero as Nigeria boosted their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with a 3-1 home win over tournament co-hosts Tanzania.

With the East Africans already assured of a spot at the finals, the Super Eagles are battling for the one qualification spot available in Group L and have little margin for error after losing 3-0 in Guinea-Bissau in September.

Alhassan Yusuf kept his composure to slot Nigeria into a second-minute lead in Uyo from Ademola Lookman's pass, but the visitors equalised through Alphonce Msanga just after the half-hour mark.

Arokodare climbed off the bench at half-time and cleverly flicked home Wilfred Ndidi's low ball to restore the lead for the West Africans in the 52nd minute.

And the Ajax striker, who is on a season-long loan from Wolves, gave the Super Eagles breathing space eight minutes later when he controlled Moses Usor's cross from the left and smashed in from 12 yards out.

With three games played in the group, Eric Chelle's side are now one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday.

Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

Elsewhere, Mohamed Salah scored twice late on against Malawi as Egypt cruised to a 5-0 victory in Ali Maher's first match in charge.

Achraf Hakimi netted two stunning goals and Yassine Bounou saved a penalty to help Morocco continue their unbeaten start with a 5-1 win over Niger.

Meanwhile, Tunisia are in danger of missing out on the finals for the first time since 1992 after suffering a 2-0 defeat at home against Libya, and Kenya scored a last-minute equaliser to end South Africa's perfect start.

The third round of qualifying culminates with three games on Saturday, while the fourth round of fixtures are split across Monday and Tuesday.

Egypt reached the semi-finals of Afcon 2025 and the last 16 of this year's Fifa World Cup under Hossam Hassan but parted company with the 60-year-old earlier this month.

The Pharaohs had taken four points from their opening two games in Group B, with Salah substituted after an hour in their 0-0 draw with Angola before missing the win in South Sudan.

The former Liverpool forward returned as captain against Malawi, and Egypt cruised into a 3-0 lead at the break through goals from Nasser Maher, Omar Marmoush and Mohamed Hany.

Salah got on the scoresheet when he stooped to head in a cross from the left and rounded off proceedings by dinking in a penalty after Hamza Abdelkarim was tripped in the box.

Victory in Maher's first game at the helm puts Egypt three points clear of Angola, who take on South Sudan on Saturday.

In Group A, Morocco had also looked like they would ease to three points against Niger in Casablanca after Yassir Zabiri's early effort and a brilliant long-range strike from right-back Hakimi put them 2-0 up after 27 minutes.

But Mohamed Abdourahmane headed in to halve the deficit and Niger had a chance to level from the spot on the stroke of half-time after a handball by Noussair Mazraoui.

However, Atlas Lions goalkeeper Bounou moved to his left to keep out Youssouf Oumarou's penalty, and Hakimi made it 3-1 in first-half stoppage time with a dipping free-kick from distance.

Youssef En-Nesyri steered in the fourth in the 77th minute from a Hakimi pass and Ayoub Oufkir completed the scoring from close range in the final minute.

Earlier in Group A on Friday Gabon beat Lesotho to move on to six points thanks to two second-half goals from Denis Bouanga.

The LA FC forward smashed the right-hand upright with a penalty but broke the deadlock with a header a minute later and then scored from 12 yards when the Panthers were awarded a second spot kick.

Tunisia downed as McCarthy frustrates Bafana

Tunisia have appeared at a record 17 consecutive Afcons but are winless and bottom of Group H - another section with just one qualifying place on offer - after defeat by their North African neighbours Libya.

The Carthage Eagles could complain about refereeing decisions going against them in Sfax, with Ali Maaloul penalised for a shirt pull on Muad Eisay just before half-time and Ali Youssef converting the resulting spot-kick.

Tunisia had a goal ruled out following a marginal offside call in the second half and three minutes later a low shot from Hamdou El Houni made it 2-0 to the Mediterranean Knights.

Libya, who last played at an Afcon in 2012, climb to second in the table and go level on points with Uganda.

South Africa are a point clear of Guinea at the top of Group D after a 2-2 draw against Benni McCarthy's Kenya in Johannesburg.

Amos Wanjala's own goal gifted the hosts an early lead before Michael Olunga levelled from the penalty spot just before half-time.

Relebohile Mofokeng restored Bafana Bafana's advantage with 13 minutes remaining, but Kenya claimed a point when Ryan Ogam's low shot from 20 yards crept inside the left-hand upright in the 90th minute.

Elsewhere, Burkina Faso joined Benin on seven points at the top of Group F thanks to Elohim Kabore's 94th-minute winner against Mauritania in Ouagadougou.

Mali extended their winning start to go top of Group K after Mamadou Camara completed a 3-2 comeback win at home against Rwanda, who had led twice in Bamako.

Rwanda had won their first two fixtures and are three points ahead of Cape Verde , who registered their first points with a 4-2 victory over Liberia in Praia.

Ethiopia registered their first win to upset Mozambique in Maputo, with Kenean Markneh scoring the only goal in the 87th minute after Mambas keeper Ernan spilled a low shot from Carlos Damtew.

The East Africans move on to three points but remain bottom of Group J, behind Sudan on head-to-head record, while Mozambique are on four points and three behind leaders Senegal.

Zambia moved level on four points with Group I leaders Algeria after a 1-1 draw at home to Burundi. The North Africans have the chance to open up a three-point gap when they host Togo on Saturday.

In Group G, Comoros were held to a goalless draw by Congo-Brazzaville in Moroni. Cameroon lead the section on seven points, with Comoros on four, Namibia on three and the Congolese bottom on two points.

articles.title: El efecto TAS en la Liga BetPlay: Así quedó la apretada pelea por el punto invisible
articles.standfirst: Fallo del TAS agita la Liga BetPlay: Cuentas y lucha total por el punto invisible
articles.summary: Fallo del TAS agita la Liga BetPlay: Cuentas y lucha total por el punto invisible
articles.body: La recta final del todos contra todos en la Liga BetPlay ha dado un giro absoluto e inesperado. Cuando la fase regular parecía encaminarse a su desenlace con una dinámica previsible, un fallo del Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte (TAS) sacudió los escritorios del fútbol colombiano y alteró de forma directa la parte alta de la tabla de posiciones. La decisión relacionada con el caso de Yhormar Hurtado —que derivó en una sanción y pérdida de puntos para el América de Cali tras un fallo a favor de Inter de Bogotá— modificó drásticamente el panorama de los clasificados y reabrió la pelea por un botín codiciado de cara a los cuadrangulares semifinales: el codiciado "punto invisible" o ventaja deportiva. Hasta antes de conocerse la resolución internacional, el conjunto escarlata manejaba los hilos de su propia clasificación y de la pugna por los puestos de vanguardia. Sin embargo, la sanción administrativa se tradujo en una resta de 3 unidades en la tabla. Con este revés, el equipo vallecaucano descendió hasta la tercera casilla con 33 puntos, un bache que no solo frenó sus aspiraciones de liderar escoltando a la cima, sino que lo dejó sin depender de sí mismo para conseguir el punto invisible en la última jornada. Panorama actual de los contendientes al punto invisible: Atlético Nacional (1.° - 39 puntos): Absoluto dominador del todos contra todos. El cuadro antioqueño aseguró la primera plaza de manera inalcanzable para cualquier perseguidor, consolidándose como el rival a vencer en el cierre del torneo. Deportivo Cali (2.° - 34 puntos): Heredó temporalmente la posición de privilegio gracias al remezón jurídico, quedando con la primera opción de abrochar la ventaja deportiva si hace los deberes en su respectivo compromiso. América de Cali (3.° - 33 puntos): Golpeado anímicamente y obligado a sumar de a tres, además de esperar una serie de resultados ajenos para aspirar al beneficio. Atlético Bucaramanga (4.° - 32 puntos): Con una campaña sumamente regular, el cuadro 'leopardo' acecha silenciosamente desde la cuarta casilla, a la espera de un tropiezo de los líderes para dar el gran golpe. Independiente Santa Fe (5.° - 31 puntos): Aunque matemático en sus opciones, el conjunto cardenal cierra el grupo de aspirantes directos con 31 unidades, necesitando una combinación de resultados casi perfecta y una diferencia de gol favorable. La fecha 19 del campeonato promete emociones a flor de piel, con transpiros cruzados y atención absoluta a los radios y pantallas de los estadios. Las matemáticas y las opciones de los principales involucrados se configuran de la siguiente manera: 1. Deportivo Cali: Depende de sí mismo Los 'azucareros' saltan a la cancha con la ventaja de la inercia numérica. Con 34 puntos, una victoria frente al Deportes Tolima les garantizará blindar el segundo puesto y quedarse con el codiciado punto invisible sin mirar otros escenarios. Cualquier otro marcador obligará al conjunto caleño a echar cuentas con los resultados de Bucaramanga y América. 2. América de Cali: Obligado a ganar y a rezar La situación de los 'diablos rojos' es compleja. Para aspirar a la ventaja deportiva, están obligados a derrotar al Deportivo Pereira, pero con eso no basta. Necesitan de manera indispensable que el Deportivo Cali no le gane al Deportes Tolima. En un escenario hipotético de empate de los americanos, la tarea se torna titánica: requerirían que el Cali pierda su juego por una diferencia de tres o más goles, apelando a la diferencia acumulada. 3. Atlético Bucaramanga y Santa Fe: Los invitados de piedra Con 32 y 31 unidades respectivamente, tanto 'leopardos' como cardenales necesitan sumar de a tres de forma obligatoria y esperar una catástrofe de los dos equipos caleños en la parte alta. Aunque sus probabilidades son más estrechas, el fútbol colombiano ha demostrado en repetidas ocasiones que los milagros estadísticos en las jornadas de cierre son una constante histórica. En el Vértice del rentado nacional, los cuadrangulares semifinales se definen por detalles milimétricos. El punto invisible —ese beneficio otorgado al segundo clasificado de la fase regular que le permite avanzar en caso de empate en puntos en la instancia de grupos— representa media clasificación a la gran final. Los equipos lo saben: arrancar la fase de los ocho con la tranquilidad de que un empate global en la serie de cuadrangulares los favorece cambia por completo el planteamiento táctico de los cuerpos técnicos. La jornada de cierre del todos contra todos no solo definirá los últimos cupos y la posición de los clasificados, sino que pondrá a prueba la resiliencia psicológica de plantones golpeados por decisiones extracancha como la del América, y premiará la constancia de instituciones como el Deportivo Cali y el Bucaramanga, que se jugarán la temporada en noventa minutos de infarto.

articles.title: El Atlético adquiere el 50% del Atlético Fútbol Club de Ecuador
articles.standfirst: El club rojiblanco se convierte en accionista, asociado con la Junta de Beneficiencia de Guayaquil, del recién ascendido a la Serie A por Carlos Santamarina, técnico de la Academia
articles.summary: El club rojiblanco se convierte en accionista, asociado con la Junta de Beneficiencia de Guayaquil, del recién ascendido a la Serie A por Carlos Santamarina, técnico de la Academia
articles.body: Del mismo modo que el Atlético con franquicias en México y Canadá de la mano del San Luis y el Ottawa, la expansión del club rojiblanco por el mundo continúa ahora por Ecuador con la adquisición del 50% del Atlético Fútbol Club, el equipo ascendido a a la Serie A el pasado mes de octubre bajo la dirección de Carlos Santamarina, técnico de la Academia. Una entrada en el accionariado de la entidad ecuatoriana, en la que compartirá el mando con la Junta de Beneficiencia de Guayaquil, que tomará cuerpo la semana que viene, cuando el consejo de administración integrado por seis miembros, tres representantes de dicha Junta y otros tres del Atlético de Madrid, se reúna por primera vez para elegir a su presidente a propuesta del club rojiblanco, así como para nombrar a un director general. Una decisión con la que el Atlético consolida el proyecto social y formativo iniciado en 2023 junto a la Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil, la entidad sin ánimo de lucro más grande del país, con el objetivo de crear una Academia e implementar el modelo deportivo y educativo del club rojiblanco en la región. Un paso más, después del exitoso ascenso logrado hace un mes, que da continuidad a los tres años que cumple el proyecto desarrollado con la Junta de Beneficencia y que se ha ido expandiendo a lo largo del país, donde acaba de inaugurarse la sede número 30, contando con presencia en 10 ciudades: Guayaquil, Cuenca, Manta, Machala, Buena Fe, Milagro, Montecristi, Salinas, Ambato y Quinindé, en las que más de 15.000 jóvenes se forman bajo el programa de desarrollo deportivo del Atlético. De hecho, a la inauguración de la sede de Cuenca, que se celebró el 14 de noviembre de 2024, asistieron el Rey de España, Felipe VI; el presidente de la República de Ecuador, Daniel Noboa; y el presidente del Atlético de Madrid, Enrique Cerezo, dando lustre a un proyecto que alcanza ahora su punto álgido con la unión del Atletico FC a la familia rojiblanca.

articles.title: ‘Benji’ Iribarne mantiene a flote a la Rojita
articles.standfirst: La Sub-21 se impone 2-0 a Japón en Almendralejo en su primer amistoso rumbo al Europeo 2027, con un Bruno Iribarne salvador, el gol de Ángel Alarcón en su debut y la sentencia de Pablo García en el 89'
articles.summary: La Sub-21 se impone 2-0 a Japón en Almendralejo en su primer amistoso rumbo al Europeo 2027, con un Bruno Iribarne salvador, el gol de Ángel Alarcón en su debut y la sentencia de Pablo García en el 89'
articles.body: Empezaba en Almendralejo el banco de pruebas rumbo al Europeo Sub-21, y el primer examen no admitía despistes. Japón, correoso como de costumbre, puso en serios aprietos a los de David Gordo y estuvo más cerca del premio de lo que dirá el marcador. Menos mal que entre los palos aguardaba Bruno Iribarne, convertido en Benji Price para la ocasión. El meta del Burgos frenó una y otra vez a los nipones, liderados por Saito, e hizo bueno el gol de Ángel Alarcón, feliz en su estreno con la Rojita, antes de que Pablo García sentenciara en el 89'. Antes del saludo protocolario, Almendralejo guardó un instante de recogimiento. Los dos capitanes depositaron un ramo de flores en el centro del campo y el estadio enmudeció en el minuto de silencio por Jesús de Miguel. Después, ya con el balón rodando, los primeros compases fueron un intercambio de golpes sin puntería, dos selecciones tanteándose sin asomarse de verdad al área contraria. El primer aviso serio lo dio Japón. Saito se plantó solo ante Bruno Iribarne y el meta del Burgos le adivinó las intenciones en el mano a mano. Pasada la media hora larga, España encontró premio en su primera acción diáfana. Umeki calculó mal un despeje de cabeza y Ángel Alarcón, el más listo de la clase en su estreno con la Sub-21, cazó el balón para batir a ras de suelo. El 1-0 llevaba la firma del debutante. La tarde se tornó negra a Umeki. Diez minutos después volvió a fallar en la salida, y en esa pelota muerta reapareció el olfato de Alarcón, que cedió a Gonzalo. El delantero quiso recortar a Kita, pero el portero le tapó un gol que ya se cantaba. Japón, lejos de rendirse a sus propios errores, siguió mordiendo en cada acercamiento. Nakajima tuvo el empate en un centro de Sato, pero su remate de cabeza se perdió por encima del travesaño. Tras el descanso, David Gordo reordenó el centro del campo en busca de respuestas nuevas. Thiago Pitarch, Mendoza y Javi Hernández entraron por Peio Canales, Iker Bravo y Marc Bernal. Aunque el plan estuvo a punto de saltar por los aires de inmediato. Saito se deshizo de Mosquera dentro del área y Bruno Iribarne le negó el empate con una mano providencial. No sería la única. Minutos después, el japonés lo intentó con un cañonazo lejano que obligó al meta a volar con otra mano prodigiosa. Acto seguido, en el córner posterior, Iribarne volvió a emplearse, esta vez con el pecho, para seguir dejando su portería a cero. Agotado por el vendaval nipón y por el protagonismo excesivo de su guardameta, Gordo recurrió de nuevo al banquillo y dio entrada a Pablo García, Mella, Espí y Dani Rodríguez. Respiró algo de calma Almendralejo, que seguía sin ver a una España especialmente inspirada en ataque. De amistoso, Japón tuvo poco. Insistió por todos los medios en busca del empate y sostuvo la presión hasta el tramo final, dueño de una segunda parte en la que fue superior. Pero el premio se lo quedó España. Ya en el 89', Pablo García se puso serio y firmó la sentencia con un zurdazo ajustado al palo corto. El 2-0 cerró el estreno de un banco de pruebas que dejó algunas dudas, pero confirmó la pegada y una seria candidatura a la portería. España: Bruno Iribarne; Iván Fresneda (Pablo García, 61'), Cristhian Mosquera (C), Yarek Gasiorowski; Álex Valle (Mella, 61'); Peio Canales (Thiago Pitarch, 46'), Marc Bernal (Rodrigo Mendoza, 46'), Iker Bravo (Javi Hernández, 46'); Ángel Ortiz (Pezzolesi, 71'), Gonzalo García (Carlos Espí, 61') y Ángel Alarcón (Dani Rodríguez, 61'). Seleccionador: David Gordo. Japón: Pisano; Kosugi, Kita, Ichihara, Umeki (Soichiro Mori, 77'), Nelson Ishiwatari (Nagano, 77'), Sato (Shimamoto, 66'), Ozeki (Yotaro Nakajima, 23'), Ishii (Yokoyama, 66'), Shiogai (C) (Shuta Sasa, 77') y Shunsuke Saito (Ishibashi, 77'). Seleccionador: Go Oiwa. Goles: 1-0, Ángel Alarcón (21'). 2-0, Pablo García (89'). Árbitro: Jérémie Pignard. Amonestó con amarilla a Yuto Ozeki (7') y Nakajima (33'). Estadio: Francisco de las Hera (Almendralejo). 11.580 espectadores. Se llevó a cabo un minuto de silencio en memoria de Jesús de Miguel.

articles.title: Competición sanciona con 12 partidos a Jesús Owono tras su expulsión ante el Tenerife
articles.standfirst: El portero del Andorra vio la roja directa en la acción en la que resultó gravemente herido Jesús de Miguel, que falleció al día siguiente
articles.summary: El portero del Andorra vio la roja directa en la acción en la que resultó gravemente herido Jesús de Miguel, que falleció al día siguiente
articles.body: El Comité de Disciplina de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol ha sancionado con 12 partidos de suspensión a Jesús Owono por su expulsión en el Tenerife-Andorra del pasado 2 de noviembre. El guardameta del conjunto andorrano vio la tarjeta roja directa en el tramo final del encuentro tras impactar con la pierna en alto sobre Jesús de Miguel cuando ambos disputaban el balón. "Doce partidos es la sanción más alta que el Código Disciplinario permite para los hechos descritos en el acta arbitral", se indica en la resolución. El árbitro, Manuel Ángel Pérez Hernández, consignó en el acta que Owono empleó una fuerza excesiva en la acción. De Miguel fue atendido sobre el césped y abandonó el campo en camilla. El delantero del Tenerife falleció al día siguiente. El Comité de Disciplina, como órgano independiente dentro de la estructura federativa, ha acordado sancionar con doce partidos de suspensión a Jesús Lázaro Ferrer Owono, jugador del FC Andorra, por la acción producida en el CD Tenerife – FC Andorra. Doce partidos es la sanción más alta que el Código Disciplinario permite para los hechos descritos en el acta arbitral. El acta es el único documento que obra en el expediente del procedimiento disciplinario y solamente con esa información sobre la acción el Comité tiene que determinar la sanción. El acta describe una acción violenta, con la pierna en alto y fuerza excesiva, cuando el balón estaba en disputa. A la vista de esas circunstancias el Comité ha considerado que los hechos se incardinan en el artículo 102 del Código Disciplinario. Asimismo, las consecuencias posteriores a la acción, que también vienen reflejadas en el acta y son públicas y notorias, han sido valoradas para agravar la sanción hasta el grado máximo permitido por la norma. En ningún caso el Comité puede superar el umbral previsto expresamente en el artículo que aplica. Contra la resolución del Comité de Disciplina, cabe recurso ante el Comité de Apelación de la RFEF en el plazo de diez días hábiles. Disciplina había aplazado la decisión al publicar las sanciones de la jornada 12 de LaLiga Hypermotion. El Juez Único de Competición dio por concluido el encuentro con el 2-2 que reflejaba el marcador en el momento de la interrupción. El Andorra retomó los entrenamientos el lunes por la tarde, una semana después del fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel tras un choque con el portero Owono. La plantilla tricolor ya se había reunido el miércoles anterior en una sesión voluntaria en la que guardó un minuto de silencio en memoria del futbolista.

articles.title: El Lega se desmelena y acaba con su mala racha a costa del Burgos
articles.standfirst: Tres goles en apenas un cuarto de hora valen el primer triunfo en ocho jornadas y primero con Carrión; incluso a Morata le anularon un cuarto tanto
articles.summary: Tres goles en apenas un cuarto de hora valen el primer triunfo en ocho jornadas y primero con Carrión; incluso a Morata le anularon un cuarto tanto
articles.body: El Leganés encontró por fin el camino de la victoria en el campeonato liguero y no sólo doblegó al Burgos con justicia y claridad en Butarque, sino que pone punto y final a su mala racha de un solo punto en las siete últimas jornadas y firma su primer triunfo liguero con Carrión. Por contra, el Burgos vuelve a caer tras cuatro jornadas sumando y podría perder su puesto en zona de 'playoffs'. Dani Rodríguez, de penalti, Oier Luengo, en propia puerta, y Álex Millán encarrilaron el encuentro en apenas media hora, mientras el debutante Irian Ribas recortó distancias en el añadido. El Leganés salió con otra actitud, más intenso, decidido y con ganas de dejar atrás su preocupante dinámica. Dani Rodríguez abrió el marcador al aprovechar el penalti cometido por Oier Luengo al darle el balón en la mano tras un disparo de Álex Sancris después de un tremendo fallo del propio central visitante... que encima diez minutos después se marcó en propia meta al desviar un centro del propio Sancris. Y apenas tres minutos después Álex Millán firmó el tercero culminando un contragolpe con un remate cruzado tras otro buen centro de Sancris. El Burgos tuvo una buena oportunidad para meterse en el encuentro, pero Dadie estrelló un balón en el poste en el minuto 35. Y en la prolongación de este primer tiempo Morata marcó un cuarto gol en el añadido del primer tiempo, pero fue anulado por fuera de juego. En la segunda parte el Burgos buscó por activa y por pasiva meterse en el partido, aunque el Leganés supo administrar su ventaja con mayor tranquilidad que en anteriores encuentros. Incluso el árbitro pitó un penalti a favor del equipo castellano por mano de Soko, pero el VAR le corrigió y no hubo pena máxima. Al final, ya en el tiempo añadido, Irian Ribas festejó su debut con el gol del honor para los burgaleses tras dejada en el área de Lencina. Así pues, una victoria necesaria, tanto por los tres puntos como por la confianza que supone para un equipo muy castigado por los últimos resultados. Butarque volvió a celebrar un triunfo liguero y el Leganés encontró, al fin, un motivo para recuperar la ilusión.

articles.title: Homenaje de Xavi al 'cruyffismo'
articles.standfirst: Países Bajos se gusta y le endosa una contundente goleada a Grecia para asegurarse el pase a los cuartos de final de la Nations League
articles.summary: Países Bajos se gusta y le endosa una contundente goleada a Grecia para asegurarse el pase a los cuartos de final de la Nations League
articles.body: No es la Países Bajos de antaño... pero Xavi Hernández le está empezando a sacar 'jugo' a esta 'Oranje'. Las sensaciones durante el parón de septiembre-octubre fueron bastante positivas... y las han vuelto a confirmar endosándole una contundente goleada a Grecia en la casa de Johan Cruyff. Reijnders brilló con un 'hat-trick' y Dumfries con otro de asistencias. Ausente por lesión en su primera lista, Xavi no dudó en darle galones de Frenkie de Jong. Dumfries, por su parte, fue titular en el lateral derecho de una Países Bajos donde, con la baja de Van Dijk, Jurrien Timber se desplazó a izquierda y Van de Ven, como en el Tottenham, formó pareja de centrales con Van Hecke. Malen fue el '9' elegido. De Jong, luciendo brazalete de capitán, trató de adueñarse del partido desde el primer momento lateralizando su posición e intercalando alturas con Timber. Fue gracias a un 'regalo' de Mavropanos en salida, sin embargo, como encontró Países Bajos la manera de adelantarse a los seis minutos. Gakpo interceptó y filtró un pase para que Summerville resolviese mano a mano cruzando ante Tzolakis. Se estaba gustando Países Bajos. La circulación de balón era bastante fluida y, pasado el primer cuarto de hora, Reijnders dejó el partido encarrilado con un doblete. Primero, resolviendo una gran combinación entre Gakpo y Veermaan 'fusilando' a Tzolakis por el primer palo y, posteriormente, empujando en área pequeña un servicio lateral de Malen. Le salía todo de cara a Países Bajos. El VAR, incluso, entró para anular un gol por mando de Ioannidis en el 24' tras una salida de terrible por parte de Verbruggen. En el 33', sin embargo, Dumfries le tiró un desmarque a Veermaan y asistió para que Reijnders firmase su 'hat-trick' particular. Quedaba tiempo antes del descanso para que Timber, en posición de '9', pusiese la 'manita' a pase de Malen. Xavi no quiso forzar la máquina con Frenkie de Jong y le dejó en el vestuario. Koopmeiners entró en su lugar y fue Veerman, que volvió a cuajar una actuación excelente con la camiseta de Países Bajos, quien pasó a llevar la batuta. El centrocampista del Barcelona sólo falló uno de los 80 pases que ejecutó. El plan de Grecia pasaba por minimizar daños y cortar la sangría. Nada más arrancar la segunda mitad, eso sí, se revisó un posible penalti sobre un Tijjani Reijnders omnipresente. Dumfries, sin embargo, sumó otras dos asistencias a su cuenta particular... cuando apenas se había superado la hora de partido. Una, de lateral a lateral, para Timber completase su doblete. La otra, para Malen después de desbordar por derecha. Todavía quedaba mucho encuentro por delante y había que empezar a mirar hacia algún 'récord'. La mayor goleada de Países Bajos fue un 11-0 a San Marino en 2011. Se agigantó Tzolakis para negarle el octavo a Summerville y evitar una goleada todavía mayor que hubiese seguido desplomando la diferencia de goles de Grecia.

articles.title: Alemania se mantiene con vida y se la jugará con la Países Bajos de Xavi
articles.standfirst: Se imponen a domicilio a la Serbia de Paunovic
articles.summary: Se imponen a domicilio a la Serbia de Paunovic
articles.body: Alemania viajaba a Belgrado con la posibilidad de poder quedarse fuera de los cuartos de final de la Nations League... a falta de disputar la última jornada. Sin embargo, hicieron los deberes contra la Serbia de Paunovic y se jugarán el pase a cuartos contra el combinado dirigido por Xavi Hernández. Cabe la posibilidad, incluso, de que haya un triple empate con Grecia en la última jornada. Klopp premió el excelso momento de forma de Gruda en el Leipzig y lo situó como extremo derecho... formando línea de mediapuntas con Wirtz y Scherhant que partían por detrás de Havertz. Treu, reforzado en el anterior parón, se agenció el lateral derecho de una Alemania donde Pavlovic y Kimmich, al igual que suelen hacer en el Bayern, formaron doble pivote. Alemania comenzó a hacer los deberes desde primera hora. A los tres minutos, bajo la torrencial lluvia que caía sobre Belgrado, Mittelstadt sirvió un centro desde el banderín de córner que, previo remate de Havertz, Babic -ex del Almería- se introdujo en propio en su intento por despejar el balón. Estaba en todas el ariete del Arsenal. Antes de llegar al primer cuarto de hora, perdonó un mano a mano ante Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. Wirtz, sin embargo, estuvo atento para recoger el rechace y duplicar la ventaja. Es el tercer gol que genera el mediapunta del Liverpool con Alemania desde la llegada de Klopp al banquillo. Tampoco estaba pisando a fondo el acelerador Alemania y, aun así, pudo irse al descanso con un par de goles más a su favor. Gruda, tras una jugada sensacional por derecha, sirvió un centro que Havertz cabeceó fuera... al igual que Thiaw a la salida de una falta botada por parte de Kimmich. Quien no perdonó, a los cinco minutos de arrancar la segunda parte, fue Gruda. Recibió la pelota en banda derecha a la altura del centro del campo, fue sorteando rivales en conducción y resolvió desde la frontal con un disparo cruzado ajustado al palo. Mejor debut imposible para demostrarle a Klopp que quiere adueñarse de la banda derecha de Alemania. Babic, previa mano de Ter Stegen a Gudelj tras una falta lateral servida por Tadic, se remidió y maquilló el marcador para una Serbia, que sin embargo, firmó su sentencia con la expulsión de Dragojeciv -había entrado al descanso- a menos de un cuarto de hora para el final por una dura entrada sobre Kimmich. Alberola Rojas fue alertado por el VAR y le mostró la roja. Zivkovic, ya en la recta final, también se fue a la calle.

Manchester United have an interest in Como midfielder Nico Paz, Chelsea are ready to target Barcelona's Jules Kounde, and Liverpool want Stuttgart's Finn Jeltsch.

articles.title: Andorra Goalkeeper Suspended For 12 Games For Collision That Leads to Player Death
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono has been suspended for 12 games after he received a red card for a reckless on-field collision with Jesús de Miguel that resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker.
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono has been suspended for 12 games after he received a red card for a reckless on-field collision with Jesús de Miguel that resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker.

The Spanish soccer federation's disciplinary committee issued the suspension for Owono on Friday, 10 days after De Miguel died a day after his clash with Owono.

The disciplinary committee said Owono used "excessive force" in the collision.

De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who rushed far outside his area, near the end of the Nov. 2 match in Tenerife. The 30-year-old De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest following the collision. He died the next day.

Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel's family.

Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

On Thursday, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again.

"He is deeply affected by the situation," Manso said. "We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return."

articles.title: France hold nerve to edge past South Africa in thriller
articles.summary: France hold on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris.
articles.body:
Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang, Attissogbe, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Lucu (3)

Tries: Wessels, Reinach, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2)

France held on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris.

The victory dents the world champions' hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts Les Bleus in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

The hosts, inspired by their captain Antoine Dupont, showed their class and skill to score three first-half tries.

France's back three of Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed in a thrilling opening 40 minutes.

The Springboks' try came before Bielle-Biarrey's, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels scoring off the back of a maul.

Number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card early in the second half for a tucked-shoulder charge, but it had the opposite effect to derailing the world champions.

Replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcolm Marx scored to set a thrilling finale, with South Africa's set-piece power proving too much.

However, Manie Libbok missed the vital conversion to Marx's try that would have levelled the game.

With South Africa pushing for a winning score, Bielle-Biarrey produced a huge defensive play to force the ball loose, before Dupont, who was named player of the match, gathered possession to help seal the victory.

The result will come as a blow to both England and Ireland, who are in direct competition with France for a place in the Nations Championship final at the end of the month.

Les Bleus, who are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings, now face Argentina next Saturday, putting them in a strong position to reach the final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November.

Injuries to France's three first-choice fly-halves - Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy - left France coach Fabien Galthie with little option but to deploy his captain and talismanic scrum-half at number 10.

Despite wearing the France number 10 shirt for the first time, Dupont lined up at scrum-half, as Galthie played Erasmus, who had again swapped his entire front row an hour before kick-off, at his own game.

It was an electric start from the hosts, as a clever move sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap, with Grandidier-Nkanang eventually crossing in the corner.

A monstrous left-footed 50:22 from Dupont, with South Africa lock Lood de Jager in the sin-bin for a high tackle, gave France the field position, before the ball cannoned off Gourgues' head and Attissogbe crossed for a fortunate try.

Dupont supplied more magic, grubber kicking through on his stronger right foot for Bielle-Biarrey to score.

South Africa's power told as they scored their opening try from a maul, before Erasmus changed his entire front row again, five minutes before half-time.

Creativity, intensity and physicality - it was a first game that felt remarkably similar to the epic quarter-final of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in Paris.

Despite losing Wiese to a 20-minute red card early in the second half, the world champions took advantage of Grandidier-Nkanang's sin-bin for a deliberate knock-on.

Tiredness and poor discipline made the game loose and chaotic, before the Springboks turned to their scrum to regain control.

A succession of scrum penalties resulted in another sin-bin, with replacement France prop Regis Montagne yellow carded as the hosts were left clinging on for the final 10 minutes.

Stunning scramble defence and sheer grit showed a side to the back-to-back Six Nations champions France that has often been questioned.

Despite their scrum crumbling, France held firm, continuing to chase kicks and compete for loose balls.

A draw would have felt a fair result given the contrasting nature of the two halves, but Libbok - as at the 2023 World Cup - badly shanked a kick that will once again raise questions over his ability to deliver under pressure in the biggest Test matches.

For once, the fine margins went against South Africa, who won every knockout game of the last World Cup by a point.

They face Ireland in Dublin next Saturday and will now likely need a favour from England, who take on New Zealand earlier that same day, if they are to reclaim top spot in the southern hemisphere standings.

France: Attissogbe; Grandidier-Nkanang, Gourgues, Moefana, Bielle-Biarrey; Dupont, Lucu; Gros, Marchand, Falatea, Verhaeghe, Guillard, Cros, Woki, Alldritt.

Replacements: Mauvaka, Neti, Montagne, Ollivon, Staniforth, Capilla, Desperes, Gailleton.

South Africa: Willemse; Arendse, Kriel, De Allende, Hooker; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, van den Berg; Steenekamp, Wessels, T du Toit, De Jager, Nortje, PS du Toit, Kolisi, Wiese.

Replacements: Marx, Nche, Louw, Mostert, Hanekom, De Villiers, Reinach, Libbok.

articles.title: Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?
articles.summary: What can Manchester United fans expect from their new manager Mauricio Pochettino? BBC Sport gets an insight from Toby Alderweireld, who played under him at...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino heads to Old Trafford with a reputation for "brutal" pre-seasons, an obsession with fitness and a no-nonsense approach.

Manchester United confirmed on Friday that Pochettino will become their manager on 18 November - replacing Michael Carrick - and has signed a contract until June 2029.

So what should the players and staff expect when the Argentine takes control at the end of next week?

BBC Sport spoke to Toby Alderweireld, who spent four years playing for Pochettino at Tottenham during a successful period where they reached the Champions League final and finished second in the Premier League.

Alderweireld, 37, says Pochettino has a no-nonsense approach to management and that he can get the best out of a squad, as long as you do it his way.

"He is very approachable but you need to follow his plan. If you don't follow his plan, you go on the side and you're not coming back any more.

"You need to think about team, team, team. If you're thinking about yourself, you're gone.

"As a player you have your own life, your own situation but he says 'look, I understand and you can talk to me about it but the team is number one' - that's the way it is and if you're not following it, he'll put you on the sideline.

"He's straightforward, has his own ideas and maybe you agree with them or don't, that's up to you. But you need to follow him and I think that's something Manchester United need - a big character, everyone in the same direction, following the plan and if not, no problem, you can go. He's the main man.

"He's a very smart man, knows how to talk to the press and what to say. He will create an environment like 'it's us against the world' - we are getting fit, we are together as a team. It doesn't matter what people say, let's work together and get results together.

"At Spurs there was coaching staff but he will be there. He knows everything. If he's not there, he's looking at video and data. He knows everything about the players on and off the pitch - the players will be watched.

"He is, in a positive way, a control freak because he says your body is your weapon and it needs to be ready to perform."

Manchester United have been criticised this season for an apparent lack of fitness and for not running enough in games - they rank in the bottom five in the league for distance covered and most high-intensity runs.

Alderweireld says Pochettino's number one demand is fitness and running .

"First of all he made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal.

"The way he wants to play - on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play - you need to run. You need to be capable of running and be capable of high intensity runs - the basic is to be fit.

"Every manager wants a good pre-season and time to give the players their ideas and the fitness. But the players are going to feel straight away that it's a different level.

"This is every day at the training ground, it's 100% - that's what he asks, what he demands. It will be a big difference for the players and they're going to see results there straight away.

"In the Champions League semi-final, we were 3-0 down [against Ajax] and he didn't have a tactical half-time talk. He just said 'you're going to be physical, you're going to fight, you only need one goal to be back in the game, believe that everything is possible'.

"That was a big moment because we were nowhere near Ajax at that time, especially in that game. But we changed everything by intensity, by duels. I remember the long ball to [Fernando] Llorente and just fighting and asking 'how badly do you want it?' It changed from that moment."

images.caption: Pochettino masterminded a comeback win over Ajax to reach the Champions League final [Getty Images]

articles.title: Tough watch as Scotland again battle against their own limitations
articles.summary: Tough watch as Scotland again battle against their own limitations
articles.body:
If Sebastien Pocognoli's honeymoon in the Scotland job ended in the wake of the defeat by Slovenia at Hampden in October, Friday night could have been the moment when all-out marital warfare broke out.

It didn't, but nobody can mistake this for peace and harmony, nobody watching Scotland pulling off a scratchy, but important, victory over North Macedonia, can have been enthused by what happened out there.

A win is a win and all of that, but this was a tough watch again, another night when Scotland battled against their own limitations. Hard graft is never a problem with this team; their passion and will to win is right up there. But nous, technical ability, belief, execution - it was a grind.

Three points against the North Macedonians was a non-negotiable. A comprehensive win against a team with no points, no goals and 10 conceded in their opening four group games would have been nice, if a little optimistic.

A draw would have been a horror show, but that's how it was looking just before the half hour. A goal apiece - and dread in heavy doses.

McGinn double gives drab Scotland win over North Macedonia

From ridicule, to relief, to remonstration

Hampden rarely stirred in a meaningful way all evening but there were three moments early in the second half that played with the emotions; from ridicule to relief to remonstration on a grand scale.

Billy Gilmour missed from point-blank range, a sitter to end all sitters, a blunder, ballooned over the crossbar, that made Chris Iwelumo's slapstick from yesteryear almost look forgivable.

Big Chris would have waited a long time to be released from the purgatory of his nightmare against Norway in 2008. He won't be, but he'll be joined in that space by Gilmour forever more. The Napoli man has, at least, many years ahead of him to atone. And it didn't cost Scotland any points on Friday. A crumb of comfort for him.

Collective groans from the stand, but then McGinn's first goal arrived and reassurance swirled around Hampden.

Scotland had a few chances in the opening half, then that gilt-edged opportunity for Gilmour, but the breakthrough had now arrived and, against North Macedonia, one goal is nearly almost enough. That's what recent history tells us.

Score once against this team and it's done. The only thing to determine at that point is how many goals you're going to win by.

That's not being disrespectful to North Macedonia. It's just reality. They had no shots on target in their opening fixture against Switzerland, one against Slovenia, zero against Scotland in Skopje and another blank in their second game against ths Swiss.

They had nothing in the first half at Hampden either, so when they scored it was a shock, a near-post header from Elmin Rastoder who got in ahead of a dozing Scott McTominay.

Rastoder ran away to celebrate, almost as stunned as Gilmour had been earlier, but for altogether different reasons. A first goal in five games in the Nations League. More than that, it was a first goal in nine all-in. The last time they had scored was a year ago in a 7-1 loss to Wales.

'Scotland looked confused and thoroughly unconvincing'

Scotland found a way to win - Ben Gannon-Doak winning a penalty and McGinn blasting it down the middle - but this was a stressful and troubling night.

McGinn's goals took him away from Hughie Gallacher in the all-time Scotland charts - and, remarkably, only six behind Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law - so there was glory in that. Fair play to him. What a momentous contribution he has made.

There was history in a 102nd cap for Andy Robertson, but you have to mine hard for the positives. Save for a few moments of coherent football. Scotland, going with three at the back again, looked confused and thoroughly unconvincing.

McGinn called it later on. Two goals for the midfielder and a whole lot of straight talking, too.

Pocognoli went with Gannon-Doak at wing-back but there were times when he didn't seem to know where he was supposed to be - a wing-back, a full-back, a winger? A square peg in a round hole.

The chances Scotland made were largely on the back of hard work rather than a functioning system dismantling a poor opponent. The entire win was down to effort rather than precision and craft or any semblance of a team knowing what they are and what they need to be doing. They triumphed over their own uncertainties.

It puts them a single point behind Slovenia with a game to go. Switzerland have won the group so that fight for second place is all that matters now.

Slovenia have the whip hand to put it mildly. They visit North Macedonia on Monday in what looks like a gimme. Scotland go to St Gallen in Switzerland. The Swiss don't need anything and might go with a second-string but it won't matter a jot to Scotland if Slovenia get it done.

They are probably going to finish third, which would make next month's draw for the Euros an exercise in crossing the fingers and hoping for mercy.

Unless there's a dramatic turnaround on the last round of matches, Scotland will be in pot three when the groups are established in Belfast in December. Pot three is not where they want to be.

Pocognoli, McGinn and Robertson all spoke in the aftermath. None sounded overjoyed, but were certainly grateful for the victory. When Rastoder scored and put the whole night in jeopardy they'd have taken an ugly 2-1. That's what they got.

Work to do, you might say. Lots and lots of it. And soul-searching, too, about systems and formations and players being shoe-horned into roles they're not entirely suited to.

A win, it's true, but heavy weather and the fear of a storm in Switzerland to come.

articles.title: Some college football teams are in flight limbo after FAA issues nationwide ground stop. Here's what to know
articles.summary: With the bulk of Week 11's games set to be played Saturday, Friday's complications are jeopardizing the scheduled slate.
articles.body:
While the sport of college football is ever-changing, especially in the NIL and transfer portal era, Saturdays still deliver their customary theater. But that reliable spectacle isn't even a guarantee for some fan bases this week.

Several teams are in flight limbo after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports on Friday. It was put into place, according to ABC News , because of a communication issue affecting air traffic control.

Baylor (playing at No. 10 BYU on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET)

Kansas State (playing at TCU on Saturday at 2 p.m. ET)

Utah (playing at No. 23 Arizona on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET)

Arizona State (playing at UCF on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET)

Ole Miss (playing at Oklahoma on Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET)

Tennessee (playing at Texas A&M on Saturday at 3 p.m. ET)

Texas (playing at No. 21 LSU on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET)

Minnesota (playing at Penn State on Saturday at 7 p.m. ET)

Purdue (playing at No. 15 Iowa on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET)

Washington (playing at Michigan State on Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET)

Oregon State (playing at No. 24 Boise State on Saturday at 6 p.m. ET)

Wyoming (playing at UTEP on Saturday at 10 p.m. ET)

North Texas (playing at UTSA on Saturday at 9 p.m. ET)

Here are other teams confirmed as grounded by Friday evening, according to On3 :

Tulane (playing at Rice on Saturday at 2 p.m. ET)

San José State (playing at Air Force on Saturday at 7 p.m. ET)

Auburn (playing at Mississippi State on Saturday at 12 p.m. ET)

Colorado State (playing at Washington State on Saturday at 10:30 p.m. ET)

Here are other teams confirmed as grounded by Friday evening, according to Sports Business Journal :

Florida Atlantic (playing at Tulsa on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET)

UNLV (playing at New Mexicon on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET)

Three teams have reportedly already pivoted to buses.

North Texas players, coaches and medical staff will be busing to UTSA, with the non-essential staff making the trip Saturday morning, according to Thamel . That game is currently scheduled for a 9 p.m. ET kickoff on Saturday.

Purdue will bus to Iowa and is expecting to arrive late Friday, per Thamel . That game is currently scheduled for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff on Saturday.

Auburn will bus to Mississippi State for the teams' 12 p.m. game on Saturday, per On3's Pete Nakos .
